reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the redline is a no-op with no counterparty comment, which is exactly what a compliant finding should look like.

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or records-examination right running against Client, and no Vendor access to Client systems; absence of any audit obligation puts us better than the playbook's preferred position, so no redline is warranted (proposing audit machinery would create a Vendor right that does not exist).

Cited paragraphs (p0047 documentation/dispute right, p0037 real-time usage statistics access) run in our favour and confirm the only information flows are toward Client, not verification rights against us.
'Missing' would be inappropriate here because the rule's purpose is to constrain a Vendor-favourable right; its absence needs no remedial clause.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause at all, not evidence of a permissive audit right.
The § 8.f anti-spam technical mechanism is correctly noted as awareness-only rather than flagged, since it operates on TrueLink's own Interface and is not an audit of Client records or systems.
